criteria.criterion: BuildMeasurement in crates/athena-data/src/records.rs gains optional peak-resident-memory and cores-used fields with serde defaults, and validate() rejects negative or non-finite values.
criteria.evidence: Read the diff: records.rs adds first/second_peak_resident_bytes: Option<u64> and first/second_cores_used: Option<f64>, each with #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]. validate() refuses cores that are not finite or are negative. The byte fields are u64, so they cannot be negative or non-finite.

criteria.criterion: BuildRun and CargoBuild::build in crates/athena-core/src/disk.rs capture peak resident memory and cores used of each cold build from the cargo process, and measure_build stores them in the record.
criteria.evidence: Read disk.rs lines 787-894 and 1070-1076. BuildRun gains peak_resident_bytes and cores_used. CargoBuild::build spawns cargo, reads stderr, then reaps it with athena_agent::procs::wait_with_usage (wait4). cores_used is CPU seconds divided by wall seconds. measure_build copies first and second into the record. The criterion is literally met, but the figures are unsound in two ways (see findings): with sccache the compiler runs outside the cargo tree, and ru_maxrss is the largest single process, not the build's total.

findings.summary: With sccache installed, the memory and cores figures leave out the compiler.
findings.evidence: When sccache is installed, the builder runs `sccache --zero-stats`, which starts the sccache server, and sets RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache. sccache clients hand each compile to that long-lived server, and the server runs rustc. The server is not a descendant that cargo waits for, so wait4's rusage on the cargo pid leaves out the compilers' memory and CPU time. Peak memory and cores used would then cover only cargo, the sccache clients, build scripts and any linker cargo starts itself. They would be far too low, and the status line gives no warning. Section 8 step 1 expects sccache runs through this same builder. Inferred from how sccache and wait4 work; no real sccache build was run here. Alternative: run the build in its own cgroup v2 and read memory.peak and cpu.stat, which count every process however it was spawned. Smaller fix: record None for memory and cores when the build is cached.

findings.summary: 'Peak memory' is the largest single process, not the build's total peak, so it understates the figure section 7 needs.
findings.evidence: ru_maxrss from wait4 is the biggest resident set of any one process in the tree. The CHANGELOG says so. Section 7.2 sizes slots by the memory of a whole build ('Two builds at about 3 GB each at CARGO_BUILD_JOBS = 2'), and cargo runs several rustc and linker processes at once, so the total can be several times the largest one. The status line prints just 'peak memory build 1 X', which a maintainer sizing slots will read as the build's total. Alternative: measure the build's own cgroup memory.peak, or poll the summed resident memory of the process tree. At minimum, label the status figure as the largest single process.

findings.summary: A changed file is outside the expected deliverables, and two planned files are unchanged.
findings.evidence: procs.rs (new unsafe wait4 wrapper and ChildUsage) is not on the deliverables list. crates/athena-core/Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock were planned but left unchanged, and the producer gave no reason. The placement looks justified: it keeps all unsafe code in the one existing module and uses the libc crate the project already depends on.

findings.summary: The old-record test builds its JSON by serializing the struct, not from a hand-written old record.
findings.evidence: The JSON comes from to_json on a struct whose new fields are None, then the test asserts those keys are absent. That is equivalent today, but a fixed old-format JSON literal would guard against future serializer changes.

findings.summary: Agent memory, which section 7.2 expects step 1 to measure, is not measured.
findings.evidence: Section 7.2 says '16 after build job 1 has measured agent memory'. The accepted reading scoped agent memory out because the acceptance names only the build record. The doc's 'Built:' note says so, so a later step still needs to measure agent memory.

summary: Fail. Every acceptance criterion is met: the four optional fields serialize correctly, old records still read, status prints the figures (and leaves them out for old records), the fake-builder test confirms they reach the committed record, and the recorded fmt, clippy and test checks passed. The measurement itself has two major soundness problems. First, when sccache is installed (the builder uses it automatically, and the design expects sccache runs), the compiler runs inside the sccache server, which is not a child of cargo. wait4 then misses its memory and CPU time, so both figures come out far too low. This is inferred from how sccache and wait4 work; no real sccache build was run. Second, ru_maxrss is the largest single process, not the build's total peak, while section 7.2 needs whole-build memory with several compilers running at once; the status line labels it just 'peak memory'. Measuring the build in its own cgroup (memory.peak, cpu.stat), or at least recording nothing for sccache builds and labelling the figure accurately, would fix both. Minor points: procs.rs changed outside the deliverables list (justified); the planned Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock were left unchanged without a reason; the old-record test builds its JSON from the struct rather than a fixed old-format literal; agent memory is left for a later step.
